headline: A multilingual scaling study reports that more experts reduce the loss penalty of broader language coverage
summary: A new arXiv preprint fits a joint scaling law for multilingual mixture-of-experts models across model size, training tokens per language, expert count and language coverage. The authors report improved prediction on held-out configurations and a smaller loss penalty when increasing coverage from 12 to 200 languages with more experts, at matched active parameters and tokens per language. These remain author-reported results from a controlled, sub-billion-parameter training grid.
